title: Pointwise relative module flatness under algebraic-space base change
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $X,Y,Y'$ be algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], and let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y'\to Y$ be morphisms. Put $X'=X\times_Y Y'$ with projections $q:X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Let $M$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module on the small etale ringed site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module] and put $M'=q^*M$, with the tensor pullback [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. Fix $x'\in|X'|$, $x=|q|(x')$, and $y'=|f'|(x')$, with point classes as in [def-a1-space-point-topology]. Relative module flatness at a point means that on every compatible etale scheme-chart diagram for the structure map the corresponding ordinary module stalk is flat over the local ring of the base chart; module flatness means exactness of tensoring [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. Then: (1) if $M$ is flat over $Y$ at $x$, then $M'$ is flat over $Y'$ at $x'$; (2) if $g$ is flat at $y'$, meaning that on every compatible etale scheme-chart diagram for $g$, as in the chart test of [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties], the chart scheme map is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] at each point lying over $y'$, and $M'$ is flat over $Y'$ at $x'$, then $M$ is flat over $Y$ at $x$. In particular, flatness of $M$ over $Y$ implies flatness of $M'$ over $Y'$. There are no finite-presentation, finite-type, proper-support or Noetherian hypotheses.

source.place: Tag 05VW (lemma-base-change-module-flat), clauses (1), (2) and the final sentence.

proof.text: Choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $b:V\to Y$, an atlas $U\to X\times_YV$, and an atlas $V'\to Y'\times_YV$, using [def-trf-algebraic-space] and [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Write $a:U\to X$, $c:V'\to Y'$, $h:U\to V$ and $k:V'\to V$ for the induced maps. Form the scheme $U'=U\times_VV'$ with projections $p:U'\to U$ and $h':U'\to V'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. It maps to $X'$, and $U'\to X'$ is surjective etale: it factors through $X\times_YV'$, with first map the base change of $U\to X\times_YV$ and second map the base change of $V'\to Y'$. The atlas compositions $a,c$ are also surjective etale by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence]. Pick $u'\in U'$ over $x'$, and put $u=p(u')$, $v'=h'(u')$, $v=h(u)=k(v')$. Then $a(u)=x$, $c(v')=y'$; in particular the charts used below are charts at the specified points.

Let $F$ correspond to $a^*M$ on $U$. The pullbacks of $M$ and $M'=q^*M$ are quasi-coherent by [lem-sfb-space-module-pullback-quasicoherent]. If $a':U'\to X'$ is the chart just constructed, the identity $qa'=ap$ and the normalized composition maps of [def-sfb-space-module-tensor-composition] identify $a'^*M'$ with $p^*a^*M$. The functorial pullback comparison in [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] therefore identifies the Zariski module corresponding to $a'^*M'$ with the ordinary scheme tensor pullback $p^*F$. Concretely the two iterated local tensors have the same image $(r\,s)\otimes m$ under the composition normalization, so this is the specified tensor pullback, with the scalar actions for $h,h'$ unchanged.

Assume $M$ is flat over $Y$ at $x$. Its every-chart definition gives flatness of $F_u$ over $\mathcal O_{V,v}$. Apply clause (1) of [lem-sfb-pointwise-module-flatness-base-change] to the cartesian scheme square $U'=U\times_VV'$ and to the quasi-coherent module $F$. It gives flatness of $(p^*F)_{u'}$ over $\mathcal O_{V',v'}$. Step 2 identifies this module with the restriction of $M'$ in the compatible charts $U'\to X'$ and $V'\to Y'$. By [lem-sfb-space-module-flat-arbitrary-charts], flatness in this one diagram implies flatness in every diagram at $x'$. Thus $M'$ is flat over $Y'$ at $x'$, proving clause (1).

Assume $g$ is flat at $y'$ and $M'$ is flat over $Y'$ at $x'$. The flat-at-$y'$ hypothesis in the statement applies to the compatible chart diagram $V'\xrightarrow{k}V$ over $g$, since $c(v')=y'$; thus $k$ is flat at $v'$. The module hypothesis gives flatness of $(p^*F)_{u'}$ over $\mathcal O_{V',v'}$ by Step 2. Clause (2) of [lem-sfb-pointwise-module-flatness-base-change] for the same scheme square yields flatness of $F_u$ over $\mathcal O_{V,v}$. By [lem-sfb-space-module-flat-arbitrary-charts] for $f$, this one diagram implies every-chart flatness of $M$ at $x$, proving clause (2). There is no assumption that $k$ is flat away from $v'$.

If $M$ is flat over $Y$, then it is flat at the image of every $x'\in|X'|$. Clause (1), already proved, gives flatness of $M'$ at every $x'$, hence flatness over $Y'$. This also covers an empty $X'$ by universal quantification.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q13-fba462498 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read Stacks 05VU, 05VW and 047C in full. The item statement matches 05VW and is unchanged from live, where the item is still unsplit; no parallel group has split it. The every-chart flatness convention is legitimate through 05VU. Step 1 builds the charts as the 05VW proof does: atlases V, U→X×_YV and V'→Y'×_YV, then U'=U×_VV'→X'. The factorisation of U'→X' is correct, and the étale-covering composition and base-change clauses come from the statements of lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence and lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers. Step 2 identifies the module on U' with p^*F, using the uniquely normalized γ of def-sfb-space-module-tensor-composition and the unconditional pullback-comparison clause of the Zariski/étale equivalence; the direct-image clause with qc/separated hypotheses is not used. Steps 3 and 4 apply 047C(1) and 047C(2) through lem-sfb-pointwise-module-flatness-base-change. In Step 4, k is flat at v' because the hypothesis on g applies to the diagram V'→V with c(v')=y'. The new node lem-sfb-space-module-flat-arbitrary-charts is exactly 05VU: some diagram if and only if every diagram, with both source and target charts free. It is true, statement-only, self-contained, not a restatement of the item, and genuinely needed because the existing chart-test nodes assume a scheme target. I tested it on a scheme target, identity charts, an étale V→Y and zero modules. My grep of the snapshot DAG for 05VU and 05VW found 23 nodes; none duplicates the new node. There are no cycles and no SGA source. Batch-5 flags: the full closures of every flagged citation contain no theorem node of sec-trace-formula or sec-poincare-duality, no nt- node and no node named for the trace formula or Poincaré duality. All are generic algebraic-space and quasi-coherent foundations, so all are accepted. No fixes.

lean.statement: theorem pointwise_module_flat_base_change {S : Scheme.{u}} {X Y Y' X' : AlgebraicSpace S} (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y' ⟶ Y) (q : X' ⟶ X) (f' : X' ⟶ Y') (sq : IsPullback q f' f g) (M : X.Modules) [M.IsQuasicoherent] : (∀ x' : Point X'.obj.obj, (ModuleIsFlatAt f M (mapPoint q.hom.hom x') → ModuleIsFlatAt f' ((moduleTensorPullback q).obj M) x') ∧ ((∀ (U : Y'.EtaleSite) (V : Y.EtaleSite) (h : U.obj.left ⟶ V.obj.left), U.obj.hom ≫ g.hom.hom = yoneda.map h ≫ V.obj.hom → ∀ u : U.obj.left.left, schemePointMap U.obj.hom u = mapPoint f'.hom.hom x' → (h.left.stalkMap u).hom.Flat) → ModuleIsFlatAt f' ((moduleTensorPullback q).obj M) x' → ModuleIsFlatAt f M (mapPoint q.hom.hom x'))) ∧ (ModuleIsFlatOver f M → ModuleIsFlatOver f' ((moduleTensorPullback q).obj M))
